issues.detail: The Hebrew lists 'וְעֵפֶר' (Epher) as the first name, but the Chinese renders it as '以弗' (Yǐfú), which is a different name. The Hebrew name is 'עֵפֶר' (Epher), not 'עֵפֶר' with a different vocalization; the Chinese '以弗' corresponds to 'Epher' but the following name 'וְיִשְׁעִי' (Yishi) is rendered as '以實基路人' (Yìshíjīlùrén), which adds '基路人' (a gentilic, 'of the road/way') not present in the Hebrew. The Hebrew has 'וְיִשְׁעִי' (Yishi), a personal name, not a gentilic. This changes the identity of the person.
